# Do the series wander? {#sec-unit-roots}

A regression of one wandering series on another finds a relationship even when
there is none. This chapter tests for unit roots in a panel. Dependence across
units, from @sec-dependence, changes which test is valid.

## First-generation tests {#sec-first-gen}

These tests assume the units are independent.

### Im, Pesaran and Shin {#sec-ips}

```r
plm::purtest(log(hp$price), test = "ips", exo = "intercept", lags = 1)
```

```
	Im-Pesaran-Shin Unit-Root Test (ex. var.: Individual Intercepts)

data:  log(hp$price)
Wtbar = 1.84, p-value = 0.967
alternative hypothesis: stationarity
```

Levels do not reject: house prices wander.

### Levin, Lin and Chu {#sec-llc}

Same call, `test = "levinlin"`. It assumes a common autoregressive root.

## Second-generation tests {#sec-second-gen}

These tests allow one common factor. The CD test in @sec-cd-test says the
factor is there.

### CIPS {#sec-cips}

```r
plm::cipstest(log(hp$price), type = "drift")
```

```
CIPS = -1.92, critical value 5% = -2.11
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Trap
CIPS under-rejects when dependence is spatial rather than factor-driven.
:::

## Summary {#sec-ur-summary}

Levels wander; growth rates do not. Estimate in differences, or check for
cointegration first.
